title: Locating a simulated configuration
statement: Let $M$ and $N$ be multi-tape Turing machines, let $e$ map configurations of $M$ to configurations of $N$, let $q$ assign a natural-number cost to each configuration of $M$, and let $X$ and $X'$ be sets of states, including the possible halting state, for $M$ and $N$, respectively. Assume that whenever a configuration $c$ of $M$ has state outside $X$, running $N$ from $e(c)$ for $q(c)$ steps yields the encoding of the next configuration of $M$; that states in $X$ encode into states in $X'$; and that each such run of $N$ stays outside $X'$ at every time strictly less than $q(c)$. If the run of $M$ from a configuration $d$ has state outside $X$ at every time $u<t$, then for every natural number $v$ at most the sum of the costs of the configurations visited by $M$ at times $0,\ldots,t-1$, there are natural numbers $u\le t$ and $w$ such that either $w=0$, or the configuration reached by $M$ at time $u$ has state outside $X$ and $w\le q(c_u)$, where $c_u$ is that configuration, and the configuration reached by $N$ from $e(d)$ after $v$ steps equals the configuration reached by $N$ from $e(c_u)$ after $w$ steps.
